artists.biography:
Baroness is a band from Savannah, Georgia whose members grew up together in Lexington, Virginia. They combine elements of sludge metal, progressive metal and punk.
Baroness formed in mid-2003, founded by former members of the punk/metal band Johnny Welfare and the Paychecks. Singer John Dyer Baizley creates the artwork for all Baroness albums, and has done artwork for other bands and labels such as Darkest Hour, The Red Chord, Vitamin X, Skeletonwitch, Sounds of the Underground, Kylesa, Kvelertak, Black Tusk, Daughters, Torche, Pig Destroyer, and the Magrudergrind/Shitstorm split grindcore CD on Robotic Empire.
From 2004 to 2007, Baroness recorded and released three EPs, named First, Second and A Grey Sigh in a Flower Husk (aka Third), with the third one being a split album with Unpersons.

perplexity.description:
Gold & Grey is the fifth studio album by American heavy metal band Baroness, released on June 14, 2019, through their own label, Abraxan Hymns. Musically, the album blends sludge, alternative, and progressive metal, showcasing the band’s signature dynamic songwriting and intricate instrumentation. The record features a diverse range of styles, from aggressive, riff-driven tracks to melodic, atmospheric passages, reflecting Baroness’s evolution and willingness to experiment within the rock genre.

As a pivotal release in Baroness’s discography, Gold & Grey marked several firsts for the band, including the addition of new members and a shift toward a more expansive sound. The album received strong critical acclaim for its ambitious scope and emotional depth, with reviewers highlighting its complex arrangements and lyrical introspection. Commercially, it debuted at No. 39 on the Billboard 200 and topped the Independent Albums chart, while also reaching No. 1 on the UK Rock & Metal Albums Chart—Baroness’s highest chart position to date.
